results.rationale: "Price of a part" fits the list price part.p_retailprice, the supply cost partsupp.ps_supplycost (what the wholesaler pays per unit), and the realized per-unit selling price from lineitem (extended price after discount over quantity). The docs don't say which one 'price' means, and the averages differ a lot (about 1,400 vs about 500).

readings.description: price = the part's list price, averaged over all parts (AVG p_retailprice)
price = the supply cost suppliers charge per unit (AVG ps_supplycost)
price = realized unit selling price on line items, l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount)/l_quantity

results.rationale: Market segment is customer.c_mktsegment, but no table stores satisfaction ratings or feedback, and none can be derived (comments are generated filler text, per the glossary's 'Free text').

links.why_not: no rating, survey or feedback column exists; comments are random generated text

results.rationale: Clerks are orders.o_clerk and 1996 sales can be computed, but the schema has no sales targets or quotas for clerks, so 'exceeded their targets' can't be evaluated.

links.why_not: no target or quota data exists for clerks; only the actual orders they handled

results.rationale: Orders in 1995 are counted on orders.o_orderdate, but the denominator 'per customer' could be only the customers who ordered in 1995 or all 15,000 customers in customer (a third of them never order, per the spec). The two averages differ materially.

readings.description: average over customers who placed at least one order in 1995 (orders only, no join)
average over all customers in the customer table, counting zero for those with no 1995 orders

results.rationale: Filter part.p_size = 50, sum partsupp.ps_availqty over each part's supplier rows, and return the 10 smallest totals. 'Available quantity' is ps_availqty per the glossary (Parts).
GERMANY is a nation.n_name value, but the nation table holds only key, name, region and filler comment; no population or demographic data exists.

links.why_not: the nation table has no population or demographic attribute

results.rationale: Average customer.c_acctbal per customer nation (nation.n_name via c_nationkey), keeping nations whose average is above AVG(c_acctbal) over all customers. Only customers are involved, so 'countries' can only be the customers' nation.

The docs don't define 'large'. It could mean high order value (orders.o_totalprice) or high quantity (lineitem.l_quantity), and any threshold is arbitrary, so different readings return different customers.

readings.description: large = orders with a high total value (o_totalprice above some threshold)
large = orders with a high total quantity (sum of l_quantity above some threshold)

results.rationale: Shipped by TRUCK is lineitem.l_shipmode = 'TRUCK', but parts have no weight attribute. p_size is a size code, not a weight.

links.why_not: no weight column exists; p_size is an integer size 1-50, not a weight

results.rationale: Shipping time is l_receiptdate - l_shipdate (glossary: Shipping time). Filter l_shipdate in 1993-1997 and customers whose nation is in region ASIA (orders -> customer -> nation -> region), then average per ship year. Grouping by ship year follows from the ship-date filter; I rejected order year as a weaker reading.
Late delivery is l_receiptdate > l_commitdate (glossary: Late delivery). Restrict to suppliers whose nation.n_name = 'INDIA' and l_receiptdate in 1993-1997, then count per receipt year.
Football results have nothing to do with the wholesale parts business the database describes.
Brand#23 is part.p_brand, but partsupp.ps_availqty is one undated value per part and supplier. No inventory history exists, so there is no month-by-month change to report.

links.phrase: available quantity … change month by month
links.why_not: ps_availqty is a single undated snapshot per part and supplier; no inventory history or dates exist

results.rationale: Late deliveries can be computed (glossary: l_receiptdate > l_commitdate), but no city is stored. c_address and s_address are random strings (spec 4.2.3), and the finest geography is nation.

links.why_not: addresses are random v-strings with no city component; geography stops at nation

results.rationale: Line items have no single date: 'in March 1996' could filter on the order date (orders.o_orderdate), the ship date (l_shipdate) or the receipt date (l_receiptdate), which give different counts. The docs don't pick one.

readings.description: line items whose order was placed in March 1996 (o_orderdate)

results.rationale: AIR shipments are lineitem.l_shipmode = 'AIR', but no freight or carrier cost is recorded. l_extendedprice is the goods' value, not shipping cost.

links.why_not: no shipping cost or carrier data exists; l_extendedprice is the value of the goods

results.rationale: Shipping mode is lineitem.l_shipmode, but nothing marks parts as fragile (p_type and p_container describe finish, material and packaging), and no damage or breakage outcomes exist to base a recommendation on.

links.why_not: no fragility attribute and no damage or breakage data exists

results.rationale: Amount paid with tax is the order total orders.o_totalprice, which the glossary (Order value; Charge) and spec 4.2.3 define as the sum of line charges including tax. Sum it per customer nation for orders with o_orderdate in 1996 and take the top 5. Stored and computed totals agree by definition. I rejected filtering by ship date, since payment attaches to the order.

Revenue is l_extendedprice*(1-l_discount) (glossary: Revenue), but 'nation' could be the customer's nation (customer.c_nationkey) or the supplier's nation (supplier.s_nationkey). Each line item has both, and they rank nations differently.

readings.description: nation = the customer's nation (where revenue is earned from)
nation = the supplier's nation (which suppliers' sales generated the revenue)

results.rationale: lineitem.l_returnflag = 'R' marks returned items, but no return reason is stored. l_comment is generated filler text (glossary: Free text).

links.phrase: reasons customers gave for returning items
links.why_not: only a returned/accepted flag exists; no reason codes or feedback are recorded
